ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: There are two triangles in the image. The large triangle on the left has vertices H, J, K; side HJ is labeled 4x+7, side JK is labeled 25, and side HK is labeled 6x-2; among them, angle H has a double-arc mark, and angle J has a single-arc mark. The small triangle on the right has vertices P, N, Q; side PN is labeled 8, side NQ is labeled 12, and side PQ is labeled 20; among them, angle N has a double-arc mark, and angle Q has a single-arc mark. From the angle marks, it can be known that ∠H corresponds to ∠N, and ∠J corresponds to ∠Q, so the remaining vertex K corresponds to P. Therefore △HJK and △NQP are similar. Corresponding sides JK and QP correspond to each other, so the ratio from the large triangle to the small triangle is 25/20 = 5/4. Side HK corresponds to side NP, and NP = 8, so HK/8 = 5/4, obtaining HK = 8 × 5/4 = 10.
